chapter: Ben Webster, Tatum and Los Angeles scene
title: Jimmy Blanton's bass playing and death
summary: He describes Blanton's revolutionary bass, his friendship with Ben Webster, and visiting Blanton in the sanitarium with TB.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah, they had those in Harlem, too. You mentioned Blanton, you first saw him in Seattle when you saw Duke. Was that the first time...?
Yeah. I met Blanton the same time I met Ben.
Was Blanton something... I mean, in terms of other bass players you had been exposed to then, was he really something...?

Oh, he was... He just scared the living daylights out of me, like he did everybody else. Because he was... He was the first bass player that ever started playing the bass that way. Everybody else was going BOOM-BOOM-BOOM-BOOM/BOOM-BOOM-BOOM-BOOM/BOOM-BOOM/BOOM-BOOM/BOOM. And he was all over that thing. And they couldn't believe it.
Ben was very fond of him, too.

Oh, they were really right. Yeah, he called Jimmy Blanton "The Bear," and Blanton called him "Frog." "Can you hear me over there, Bear?" "I hear you down there, Frog." Ben almost tore Chicago apart the night that he heard about Blanton... Because they put Blanton in a sanitarium, in a single room -- it was like putting him in a cell. Everything was white and clean. All there was, was
Rowles - 37
just a picture of Ben Webster on the dresser and a clock. That was it.
Did you see him there?
Yes, I drove out there to see him. He couldn't even feed himself. They put the tray here; you know, the nurse would feed him.
He was so weak by then?
Yeah. If it happened in these days, they could have saved him.
Of course. The same with Charlie Christian.
Sure.
And now TB is...

Too bad. Jimmy Blanton was a wonderful person. And I should have gotten a picture of Jimmy. He used to play, you know, in these clubs in Seattle; he'd play and work up a terrible seat, he'd put on his overcoat and walk out the door with it hanging open. And Ben used to tell him, 'Button it.' He said, 'Button up your coat. It's chilly out here. Windy. Button up.' But he'd never do it. I was too young. I didn't know to think anything of it. So when he got TB ...(?)... See, on top of that, he didn't drink.
He didn't.
No. And Ben, you know, could make up for
Rowles - 38

everybody. Consequently, when he went outside, he was so warm that he could have gone around with just a pair of shorts on and it wouldn't make a difference. I didn't drink either -- or smoke. I didn't start smoking until I was 23. I started drinking when I joined... I really started drinking when I joined Lee and Lester Young. [COUGHS]
